classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part requires recognising that the 30 extra sweets represent the single-part difference between 3 and 2, then scaling to the five-part total. Other parts require choosing the appropriate known share or total as the unitary starting point.

content.prompt: Marta and Faith share some sweets in the ratio $3:2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If there are 30 sweets altogether, how many do they each get?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3+2&=5\text{ parts}\\1\text{ part}&=30\div5=6\text{ sweets}\\3\text{ parts}&=6\times3=18\text{ sweets}\\2\text{ parts}&=6\times2=12\text{ sweets}\end{align*}$$
Marta gets 18 sweets and Faith gets 12 sweets.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If Marta gets 30 sweets, how many sweets were there altogether?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}3\text{ parts}&=30\text{ sweets}\\1\text{ part}&=30\div3=10\text{ sweets}\\5\text{ parts}&=10\times5=50\text{ sweets}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: If Faith gets 30 sweets, how many sweets does Marta get?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2\text{ parts}&=30\text{ sweets}\\1\text{ part}&=30\div2=15\text{ sweets}\\3\text{ parts}&=15\times3=45\text{ sweets}\end{align*}$$
Marta gets 45 sweets.

children.label: d
children.prompt: If Marta gets 30 more sweets than Faith, how many sweets were there altogether?

answer.worked:
The difference represents $3-2=1$ part.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ part}&=30\text{ sweets}\\3+2&=5\text{ parts}\\5\text{ parts}&=30\times5=150\text{ sweets}\end{align*}$$
